Subject: Eastward Payments - post-upgrade latency & error spike

Team — flagging an urgent customer signal from Eastward Payments (deal D-45922). They rolled our v3.4 + qprofile-beta2 yesterday night and are now seeing a large hotpath impact. High level: p95 increased ~5x on their payment validation route, 5xx rate up ~1.6% (was 0.02%), and overall throughput fell ~18% under normal traffic.

Attached: p95 traces and hotpath logs I pulled from their dashboard. I also pasted the alert snippets below.

Alert snapshot:
- Route: /v1/pay/validate (heavy short-sequence traffic)
- Baseline p95: 220ms -> observed 1.1s at peaks (sustained)
- 5xx spikes: 0.02% -> 1.6% (mostly 5xx decode failures + kernel timeouts)
- Throughput: nominal 0.9k rps -> 0.74k rps (20% drop)

Customer impact: blocking some merchant flows during US morning. They are asking for an immediate mitigation and exec contact. Jill Park (acct owner) is already on the phone with our support team.

Immediate asks:
1) Rishi — can you triage kernel/quant interaction quickly and advise if a rollback to v3.3 or switching to v3.4-fp16 is safer?
2) Marissa — can you coordinate a customer call and confirm if they want a rollback or a canary of the fp16 variant?
3) I'll loop in CRO/CTO if we need exec attention and credits.

Attaching: eastward-p95-traces-20270630.csv, hotpath-logs-20270630.txt

-ben

Quick triage notes — replicated locally against a small snapshot of Eastward traffic:
- Root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel (qprofile-beta2) is triggering a fallback path in the attention kernel for short-seq workloads on the customer's T4 fleet. The kernel selection is timing out under their sequence-length distribution, leading to extra CPU fallback and occasional decode errors when mixed with our new CUDA routine.
- Evidence: elevated kernel boundary logs and ~120ms extra scheduling latency in the KV-cache warm path. Logs show increased error stacktrace entries in the quant decode layer (attached sample).

Mitigation options (ordered by speed/risk):
1) Rollback to v3.3 (unquantized) — low risk, fastest (estimated 10-20 minutes to full rollout). Restores previous kernel path.
2) Patch qprofile to force fp16 kernels for short sequences — medium risk, will need a quick bake (30-60 minutes).
3) Canary v3.4-fp16 variant for 10% traffic — low-risk test prior to full flip; requires routing rule change.

I recommend immediate rollback (1) as the default to stop customer impact and buy time for a robust qprofile fix. If leadership wants to avoid a rollback, option 3 gives a safer immediate alternative.

Runbook excerpt: 1) Trigger rollback job: runbooks/model-rollback-playbook -> step 2 (rollout restore) 2) Monitor p95 and 5xx on the Eastward route for 20 minutes 3) If stable, schedule a controlled re-deploy with patched qprofile.

I’m standing by to execute rollback if Marissa/Jill confirm.

—Rishi
